definitions.change_verdict: a verdict of persistent change, abrupt change or gradual drift, which the pipeline can raise a behavioural alert about. The alert policy is not applied
definitions.deviating_day: an evaluable day whose deviation is at or past the threshold in absolute value
definitions.evaluable_day: a day the baseline gives a verdict on other than insufficient data: from the day 14 others are retained
definitions.found: a series with a change verdict on a day from 56 to 76. Where nothing was added this is a false report, and where a ramp was added it began 14 days before the window opens
definitions.needed_threshold: the value a Gaussian day's deviation from the median of n other days, in units of 1.4826 times their MAD, exceeds in absolute value as often as the nominal rate of the declared threshold. The floor on the scale is not applied
definitions.nominal: the share of Gaussian values at or past the threshold in absolute value, which is what the threshold states

matching.same_detection: the largest multiple at which the calibrated reference finds the step of two standard deviations in at least as many series as the default does at its declared thresholds; the smallest multiple if there is none
matching.same_false_reports: the smallest multiple at which the calibrated reference reports a change, with no step added, in no more series than the default does at its declared thresholds; the largest multiple if there is none
matching.why: this is the rule the threshold-calibration protocol applies to its tuning homes, so that what it finds there can be set against what Gaussian days give

configuration.name: threshold-null
configuration.pairing: every reference, shape and threshold is run on the same series, so two of them differ in the reference, the shape or the threshold alone

references.calibrated: `BaselineConfig.calibrated`: the same centre, a scale pooled over every retained day, and the deviation mapped through a Student t on 0.368 degrees of freedom for each day behind the scale
references.default: the default: the centre and the scale are the median and the MAD of the days of the same weekday once 4 exist, and of all the days before that

configuration.seeds: the series of block b for purpose p come from `numpy.random.default_rng([seed_root, p, b])`, in blocks of 100; p is 0 for the rates, 1 for the operating points and 2 for the needed thresholds

shapes.ramp2: 2 standard deviations are taken off gradually, from day 42 over 28 days
shapes.step2: 2 standard deviations are taken off from day 56
shapes.step3: 3 standard deviations are taken off from day 56
shapes.weekend: 1.5 standard deviations are added to every Saturday and 2 to every Sunday: a weekly rhythm and no change
shapes.weekend_step2: the weekly rhythm, and 2 standard deviations taken off from day 56

configuration.standard_errors: a share of days is a ratio over series, and its standard error treats the series as the unit, since the days of one series share a history. A share of series has the binomial standard error, and a paired difference the standard deviation of the differences over the root of their number
configuration.status: a measurement on synthetic values, made to design and to check the calibrated reference. It tests nothing about a home
configuration.thresholds: at scale s the deviation threshold is 3 s and the trend threshold 3.5 s
configuration.values: independent draws from one Gaussian with standard deviation 1 around 8, one a day, given to `AdaptiveBaseline` directly. No home is simulated and no state is inferred
what_was_seen_before: the calibrated reference was designed on series of this kind, drawn from other seeds. The 0.368 degrees of freedom for each residual were settled in exploratory runs that are not recorded

this measurement was made once before in full, from another root and with fewer multiples, when the calibrated reference fitted its trend to the days as they are. With a weekly rhythm added it then reported a gradual drift more often, as the default does. Its trend was changed because of that, to be fitted to each day's distance from its own weekday, and a shape with both a rhythm and a step was added. That first record is not published
none of the series here was used to choose anything

evidence.reason: no state is inferred: synthetic daily values are given to the baseline directly, one a day, and each is judged before it joins the history

inference.label: online filter
inference.provenance: declared by the experiment that wrote the record

metric_definitions.evaluable_day: a day the baseline gives a verdict on other than insufficient data: from the day 14 others are retained
metric_definitions.found: a series with a change verdict on a day from 56 to 76. Where nothing was added this is a false report, and where a ramp was added it began 14 days before the window opens
metric_definitions.needed_threshold: the value a Gaussian day's deviation from the median of n other days, in units of 1.4826 times their MAD, exceeds in absolute value as often as the nominal rate of the declared threshold. The floor on the scale is not applied

notes: The values are synthetic: independent Gaussian days, with a step, a ramp or a weekly rhythm added where a shape says so. No home is simulated and no state is inferred, so nothing here is evidence about a home.
A measurement, not a test. It was made to check the calibrated reference where the answer is known. The series here were not used to choose anything.
Change verdicts are counted, not alerts: the alert policy is not applied.

10,000 series are behind the rates and 2,000 behind the operating points, all derived from one recorded root. docs/SIMULATION_PROTOCOLS.md sets a floor of 100, and every share is given with its standard error.
